title: Murphy Vs. Pico Odds, Full Fight Preview & Prediction
text: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Featherweight contenders Lerone Murphy vs. Aaron Pico will collide this weekend (Sat., Aug. 16, 2025) at UFC 319 inside United Center in Chicago, Illinois. Is it possible to be a dark horse contender while riding an eight-fight win streak? Murphy has beaten quite a few excellent fighters in recent years, but his decision-heavy style and relative inactivity has slowed his would-be rise. It’s getting harder and harder to deny “The Miracle,” however, and facing an exciting newcomer should help garner more attention. Pico has pretty much been raised since birth to be a fighting champion. An outstanding amateur wrestler with lots of elite international experience, Pico spent much of his youth boxing as well. In the cage, he’s a tremendous finisher with vicious power, and his only loss in his last 10 fights happened because of a dislocated shoulder. Let’s take a closer look at the betting odds and strategic keys for each athlete: Murphy vs. Pico Betting Odds - Lerone Murphy victory: +205 - Lerone Murphy via TKO/KO/DQ: +650 - Lerone Murphy via submission: +2800 - Lerone Murphy via decision: +250 - Aaron Pico victory: -250 - Aaron Pico via TKO/KO/DQ: +330 - Aaron Pico via submission: +900 - Aaron Pico via decision: +140 - Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook How Murphy Wins There are serious shades of Leon Edwards to Lerone Murphy’s game … and I say that in both a positive and negative way. He’s a really accurate and tricky range striker, able to force opponents into his preferred kind of kickboxing match. His wrestling is quite good offensively and defensively. Yet, when he does find an edge, it doesn’t always feel like Murphy takes full advantage. Footwork and kicking ability are Murphy’s edge here. As he just did versus Josh Emmett, Murphy has to deny the pocket and keep his back off the fence. He’ll be playing the matador, trying to force Pico to continually reset and refuse him the chance to unload power punches. Murphy has to be really effective with his linear strikes here. His usual game plan of stick-and-move applies, but that “stick” better be impactful. He’s not going to scare Pico off unless he really sits on his jabs, intercepting right hands, snap kicks, spin kicks, knees up the middle — something has to gain Pico’s respect. Otherwise, the hyper athletic Pico will surge forward and dictate where the fight takes place. How Pico Wins At age 28, Pico already has a wealth of world-class experience in competition. From wrestling to Pankration to boxing to his years in Bellator, Pico has been preparing for a run at the top for a lifetime, and he’s finally in a position to put it all together. There’s a reason he’s been called the greatest prospect in MMA more than once. I’d like to see Pico building on the success Emmett found against Murphy. They have similar strengths — punching power and wrestling — but Pico is a bit quicker on his feet. He should be able to find Murphy more often and create exchanges, which will help to get his wrestling going as well. It’s really important that Pico finds some success with his takedowns. He has to put Murphy in a defensive position, give him a reason to hesitate in firing kicks. The more Pico can convince Murphy to withdraw into himself, the easier this fight will be. Ripping combinations is certainly one way to do that, but a big lift and slam will sway judges and limit Murphy’s activity effectively too. We’ve see Pico neglect his wrestling to his own detriment previously. There’s no need to make this match up harder! Murphy vs. Pico Prediction I’m expecting a close fight here. Murphy is difficult to take down, and he’s the more polished striker. His evasive movement and commitment to staying in good position should take a significant portion of the sting of Pico’s big swings, so the early KO doesn’t feel very likely. Meanwhile, Pico has never beaten anyone particularly decent via decision, so this will be a real test of whether he can manage his aggression and output against a savvy fighter successfully. Ultimately, Murphy is likely to win more of the fight, but Pico will have the bigger moments. In a five-rounder, that kind of attritional success would favor Murphy. In a 15-minute fight, that’s not the case. Pico only has to score a couple big takedowns or a knockdown to dramatically change the judges’ scorecards and erase minutes of Murphy success, which reads like a problem against a fighter content to win on thin margins. Prediction: Pico via decision MIDDLEWEIGHT TITLE CAR CRASH! title: Ex-UFC star has 'no idea' why Aaron Pico took UFC 319 debut against undefeated contender
text: Not everybody is a fan of Aaron Pico’s new UFC debut. Former Bellator star Pico is one of the brightest prospects we’ve seen in recent memory. The 28-year-old is 13-4 (9 KO) as a pro and is a former amateur golden gloves boxing champion and medalist in freestyle wrestling. Pico turned his career around after suffering a massive upset loss in his MMA debut. Pico signed to the UFC earlier this year and was supposed to debut against the undefeated #1 contender Movsar Evloev at UFC Abu Dhabi this weekend. Unfortunately, Evloev withdrew and on Saturday, the UFC announced a new opponent and date for Pico. Pico will now face the 16-0 Lerone Murphy at UFC 319 on Aug. 16, in Chicago, Illinois—the co-main event to middleweight champion Dricus du Plessis vs. Khamzat Chimaev. A former fighter doesn’t understand why Pico accepted this fight. Josh Thomson says Lerone Murphy ‘tougher fight’ for Aaron Pico than Movsar Evloev England’s Murphy is primarily a striker, a totally different style matchup than the grappling-heavy Evloev. Murphy is ranked five spots below Evloev and hasn’t yet cracked the top-5 despite defeating perennial contender Josh Emmett in his first main event in April. Murphy’s undefeated at 16-0-1 and he has eight straight wins in the UFC. Former Strikeforce Champion and UFC lightweight Josh Thomson thinks Pico might have made a mistake going up against Murphy. “I have no idea why you took this fight,” Thomson said of Pico on the Weighing In Podcast. “You went from Evloev, who’s basically considered to be the number one contender. “Stylistically, this is a tough fight,” Thomson said of new opponent Murphy. “I’m not saying that Aaron can’t win this fight. This is a tougher fight for him than the Evloev fight. I wanted to see the Evloev fight because the two of them can wrestle. The boxing favors Pico a little bit. “That’s the fight that I always wanted to see, so I’m being sour right now,” Thomson continued. “But the Lerone Murphy fight, to me, Pico’s gonna have to close that distance. He cannot let Lerone Murphy stay on the outside. He’s got to close that distance, get in there. I think he has the opportunity to take him down, but he’s gonna take some shots coming in…” Movsar Evloev could potentially get next title shot 19-0 as a pro and 9-0 in the UFC, it’s getting pretty hard to deny Movsar Evloev of a title opportunity. The #1 UFC featherweight contender is coming off wins over former champion Aljamain Sterling, Arnold Allen and Diego Lopes, who fought and lost to Alexander Volkanovski for the title at UFC 314 in April. One of the only things that has prevented Evloev from a title opportunity is likely his lack of finishes, with all nine of his UFC victories coming by way of decision. Still, the champion Volkanovski has vouched for Evloev to be his next challenger on multiple occasions.

title: Ex-UFC star has 'no idea' why Aaron Pico took UFC 319 debut against undefeated contender
text: Not everybody is a fan of Aaron Pico’s new UFC debut. Former Bellator star Pico is one of the brightest prospects we’ve seen in recent memory. Pico signed to the UFC earlier this year and was supposed to debut against the undefeated #1 contender Movsar Evloev at UFC Abu Dhabi this weekend. Pico will now face the 16-0 Lerone Murphy at UFC 319 on Aug. 16, in Chicago, Illinois—the co-main event to middleweight champion Dricus du Plessis vs. Khamzat Chimaev.
